steps.text: Pour warm water into a container that is twice the volume of the water.
Add salt, soy sauce, sugar, and olive oil; stir until sugar and salt have dissolved.

Allow brine to cool to room temperature. This chicken brine recipe results in perfectly tender and flavorful chicken every time. Plus, it comes together quickly with just five ingredients you probably already have on hand! This recipe proves a dish doesn't need to be complicated to be delicious. Four common kitchen ingredients and a bit of time and you'll have restaurant-worthy chicken ready for a thousand different applications.

raw_recipe.headline: Simple Chicken Brine
raw_recipe.description: Just a simple chicken brine to help make the meat just a little more tender and juicy. This recipe was made for roughly a 6 pound whole chicken.

video.description: This video shows you how to make a simple brine for roasted chicken. Kosher salt, sugar, soy sauce, and a little olive oil create an easy soaking solution for whole chickens. The result is a roasted bird that’s always super moist, tender, and flavorful.

review.reviewBody: Really good and really easy! The chicken was sooooo tender. However, if you plan to cook your chicken in a slow cooker, you're going to need to shorten your cooking time if you brine. Otherwise, the chicken will just fall apart. I was worried that the soy sauce would overpower it but not at all. Everyone loved it and said it was their favorite so far. I cook a chicken about once a week and am always trying different recipes. This is definitely a keeper!

I use this brine a lot for 5 lb whole chickens. When roasting in the oven, I cook at 450 for 15 min, then at 350 for 1.5 hours. I baste it with paprika, butter and salt mixture every 30 minutes. Comes out so tasty and moist! The only thing I change about the brine is lower the olive oil to about one tablespoon. I've also used this brine for beer can chicken which is just as good.

Made this exactly as written and soaked a 5 pound chicken for 3 hours. I did use low sodium soy sauce because that is what I had on hand. Would have been good brining a little longer, not too salty. Rubbed with butter and sprinkled with garlic powder and poultry seasoning before roasting. Did not rinse before roasting at 450 for 15 minutes and then 350 for an hour. Perfect. Will make again.

I cut this recipe in 1/2 for 2 pkgs of chicken thighs (about 4 lbs)
I marinated for 3.5 hours.
Then I grilled them -on charcoal - 5 mins each side.
They came out perfect and moist. Not dry at all. The soy sauce could be dialed back if you want then to be less salty.
I used less sugar. I added orange rind and peppercorns. I rinsed before cooking. A very significant improvement on roasting without this step. I used Mark Bittman roasting method.

Made it as the recipe said and it works fine. Only thing I changed is I left out the oil the second time I made it.
Real olive oil just coagulates and floats on the top of the brine, a waste of EVOO. I prefer to put the oil on the bird after I rinse off the brine and right before it goes in the oven.
I use canola oil in my marinade when it calls for olive oil, for the same reason, it doesn't harden as it gets colder.

I followed the measurements exactly as listed but I added some whole peppercorns and about 1tsp of herbs de Provence. I bribed my chicken for about 5 hours. I did not rinse my chicken after. I cooked my chicken rotisserie (set it and forget it) and crammed a half yellow onion (quartered) and a small apple (quartered) inside. It was delicious!! The meat throughout was flavorful and perfect.

This brine makes ALL the difference in the world to roast chicken. Even the breast meat comes out juicy and tender. I use a 2 gallon resealable bag to hold the chicken and the brine, then place it all in a large plastic bowl (in case the bag leaks) and refrigerate for 1-2 days. YUM!

I think many people that gave this a low ratingmight not know the difference between brine and marinade. This is fast and simple. Keeps chicken moist and prevents overcooking. After rinsing the brine off and patting dry with papertowels, it's sinless enough to add any dry rub or throw into a quick marinade of your choice. ty

Keeper recipe and highly recommend u try it too! simple and delicious. Brined 2 chickens (1.2kg each) with this recipe (omitted oil in brine) for 2 hours only, forgot to rinse the excess brine, but it came out perfectly flavoured and super juicy. Trick I did to get the flavours into the meat asap , was to spatchcock the chicken, then lift the skin away from the flesh and puncture the breasts, legs and thighs. Roasted the chicken on a bed of carrots, onions,and the removed spine. We had the thighs for dinner, breast meat for tomorrow's sandwiches and the beautifully roasted bones and carcass , carrots and onions made a wonderful stock!

This is a very simple brine and it is quite good as is. I made some changes to modify the flavor. I use half the amount of dark soy sauce in place of the regular soy sauce and use half a cup of tender quick instead of the kosher salt. The result is super moist and very flavorful chicken.

I brine a whole chicken with the recipe every Saturday night. Then cook it on a Kamado Joe grill at 300° with some Apple and Cherry wood for delightful smoke flavor. This brine is a game changer when it comes to cooking a whole chicken.

Wow, 9 years later. (Update) This is still my go to Brine for Chicken. I use it for whole chicken and quartered chicken when grilling or rotisserie. Chicken IS ALWAYS Moist. I do use the recipe as is for my base. For extra flavor I do like to add Rosemary and some garlic cloves. For the container i use a soft sided cooler insert.

I've been using this brine for all poultry, including turkey, duck, quail and dove. I have cooked on propane, PBC barrel, 26 Weber, Smokn'Tex Smoker, and various dishes in the oven. It's the absolute BEST. Very simple and quick to put together. Toss in Ziplock bag and into the frig. I've done 3 hours up to 3 days. In my opinion, overnight is just about perfect. You can spend a lot more money, but you won't get as good as results. This brine does NOT cover the flavor of the meat, but makes it "bettah". I was going to have this recipe tatooed on my forearm, but it's so simple, even my peabrain can remember it.
Very useful as is. I sometimes add my favorite hot sauce which gives a nice kick.

Two times using 2 5lbs whole chickens. And each one was so tender and the flavors were wonderful with the addition on a few more seasonings for tge brine. This my go to recipe from now and forever. 🙏🙏☝️

If you know what a true “yard bird” is then you know it’s tough. This brine made it tender and was absolutely not to salty as some state. 5 hrs brine, pulled out of brine and in clean Dutch oven sautéed onions and garlic. Added I can of dieced tomatoes along with real butter . Sason, adobo, pepper! 1.5 hrs at 325 Wonderful!!!!!!

Great basic brine! I use this all the time when I buy chicken breasts in bulk. Then dry them and vacuum seal. Only thing I would watch out for is don't leave it in too long, it can get a bit salty. Sometimes I'll dilute with another quart of water.
